errors.claim: three incompatible pressure normalizations ... \hat p = p/(\rho_\infty a_\infty^2) \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1/\gamma ; alternative \hat p = p/(\gamma p_\infty) \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1/\gamma ; alternative \hat p = p/p_\infty \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1
errors.problem: The first two are the SAME normalization: a_\infty^2 = \gamma p_\infty/\rho_\infty, so \rho_\infty a_\infty^2 \equiv \gamma p_\infty identically. Only two distinct conventions are listed, not three, and calling them 'incompatible' is wrong for that pair.
errors.correction: The genuinely distinct set is: \hat p = p/(\rho_\infty a_\infty^2) = p/(\gamma p_\infty) \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1/\gamma; \hat p = p/p_\infty \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1; and (the omitted third, very common in CFD) \hat p = p/(\rho_\infty U_\infty^2) \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1/(\gamma M_\infty^2).

errors.claim: the temperature generator is either T_\infty or the recovery temperature; the two differ by (\gamma-1)M^2/2
errors.problem: They differ by the FACTOR 1 + r(\gamma-1)M^2/2 (r = recovery factor; r=1 gives the stagnation temperature T_0/T_\infty = 1+(\gamma-1)M^2/2). The quoted expression is only the excess term and is wrong if used as a ratio — it tends to 0, not 1, in the incompressible limit.
errors.correction: T_r/T_\infty = 1 + r(\gamma-1)M_\infty^2/2, with r \approx Pr^{1/2} (laminar) or Pr^{1/3} (turbulent); T_0/T_\infty = 1+(\gamma-1)M_\infty^2/2.

errors.claim: R declared as a generator with numeric_factor 1 (emits R), together with per_symbol '\hat T = T/T_\infty' and the note '\Theta becomes an active basis dimension here'
errors.problem: Mutually inconsistent. Absorbing R eliminates \Theta exactly as k_B=1 does; with a_\infty as the velocity generator the resulting temperature unit is a_\infty^2/R = \gamma T_\infty, so \hat T_\infty = 1/\gamma, not 1. One cannot simultaneously set R=1, keep \Theta active, and have \hat T_\infty = 1.
errors.correction: Pick one: (i) R absorbed \Rightarrow \Theta dead, temperature unit a_\infty^2/R, \hat T_\infty = 1/\gamma (or 1/(\gamma M_\infty^2) if U_\infty is the velocity generator); or (ii) T_\infty declared as the \Theta generator \Rightarrow \Theta active, \hat T_\infty = 1 and R survives as the residue \hat R = RT_\infty/a_\infty^2 = 1/\gamma.

errors.problem: The entry's own per_symbol row states that \hat\theta = (T-T_\text{ref})/\Delta T is an additive offset, 'outside the multiplicative generator formalism entirely', and the notes call it 'the one place in the whole family where the multiplicative generator table genuinely cannot express the convention'. A pure-quotient verdict therefore understates what the schema must carry — milder per-symbol riders (e.g. B/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0} in the MHD entry) were classified needs_symbol_rescaling.
errors.correction: schema_fit should be needs_symbol_rescaling (with the affine T_\text{ref} offset flagged as outside the multiplicative group), not needs_custom_generators. All physics claims in this entry — \nu/(U_fH)=\sqrt{Pr/Ra}, \kappa/(U_fH)=1/\sqrt{RaPr}, unit buoyancy coefficient, \tau_f=H/U_f — recompute correctly.

errors.claim: \beta_\text{ref} = 8\pi n_\text{ref}T_\text{ref}/B_\text{ref}^2 (Gaussian-rooted, GENE) vs 2\mu_0 nT/B^2 (SI-rooted) — why: 'factor-of-4\pi discrepancy in the electromagnetic residue'
errors.problem: \beta is dimensionless and takes the SAME numerical value in both systems; the two expressions are one quantity written in Gaussian and in SI, because B is measured in different units in each. There is no 4\pi discrepancy in the residue. Stating one invites a converter to apply a spurious 4\pi correction to a convention-independent number.
errors.correction: Both formulas give identical \beta. The actual trap is a formula/units mismatch — inserting SI-valued n, T, B into 8\pi nT/B^2 (or Gaussian values into 2\mu_0nT/B^2). Record it as a units-of-input hazard, not as a factor in the residue.

errors.claim: gyrokinetic quasineutrality: \sum_s \hat q_s(\int \hat f_s d^3\hat v - \hat n_s\hat q_s\hat\phi/\hat T_s) = 0
errors.problem: As written the second term is the adiabatic (Boltzmann) response; the gyrokinetic polarization density carries the gyroaverage / (1-\Gamma_0(b_s)) factor, and the first integral is over the gyro-averaged distribution, not f_s.
errors.correction: \sum_s q_s\int J_0\hat f_s d^3\hat v = \sum_s (q_s^2 n_s/T_s)(1-\Gamma_0(b_s))\hat\phi, b_s = k_\perp^2\rho_s^2; the entry's form is the b_s\to\infty / adiabatic simplification.

verdicts.system: Gyrokinetic normalization, GS2 / stella / AstroGK family

errors.claim: coulomb: 'the implied form is \hat U = \hat q_1\hat q_2/(4\pi \hat r) in SI-rooted normalization or \hat q_1\hat q_2/\hat r in Gaussian-rooted normalization'
errors.problem: Recomputing with the entry's own normalizations (charges in e, lengths in d_e = c/\omega_{pe}, energies in m_ec^2): U/(m_ec^2) = [e^2\omega_{pe}/(4\pi\varepsilon_0 m_ec^3)]\,\hat q_1\hat q_2/\hat r, and using e^2/\varepsilon_0 = m_e\omega_{pe}^2/n_0 the prefactor is 1/(4\pi n_0 d_e^3). A large dimensionless plasma-parameter residue survives; the pair Coulomb energy is NOT unity-normalized the way the field equations are.
errors.correction: \hat U = \hat q_1\hat q_2/(4\pi n_0 d_e^3\,\hat r) (SI-rooted), i.e. \hat U = \hat q_1\hat q_2/(\hat r\,\cdot 4\pi N_{d_e}) with N_{d_e}=n_0d_e^3 the number of particles per skin-depth cube — the same residue that governs the (deliberately unphysical) macro-particle collisionality of a PIC run.

errors.claim: gauss_law derivation: '... = e n_0\hat n/\varepsilon_0 = m_e\omega_{pe}^2\hat n'
errors.problem: Algebra slip: en_0/\varepsilon_0 = m_e\omega_{pe}^2/e, not m_e\omega_{pe}^2 — the intermediate expression is dimensionally inconsistent with the LHS (m_e\omega_{pe}^2/e)\nabla\cdot\hat E.
errors.correction: ... = e n_0\hat n/\varepsilon_0 = (m_e\omega_{pe}^2/e)\hat n, whence \nabla\cdot\hat E = \hat n. The stated conclusion is right; only the middle step is wrong.

verdicts.system: GRMHD code units (G = c = M = 1 plus an independent density/accretion scale)

errors.claim: schema_fit: needs_custom_generators, with a fifth 'generator' listed as '4\pi absorbed into B', dimension (0,0,0,0,0), numeric_factor 4\pi
errors.problem: Two problems. (i) B_\text{code} = B_\text{Gauss}/\sqrt{4\pi} is a genuine per-symbol redefinition not derivable as a quotient of (G, c, M_\text{BH}, \mathcal{M}_\text{unit}); the identical rescaling in the Newtonian MHD entry was correctly classified needs_symbol_rescaling. (ii) The fifth entry is a dimensionless 'generator' — exactly the construct the enumeration's own h-units entry declares unsupportable in a generator table (zero row in the restoration matrix).
errors.correction: schema_fit = needs_symbol_rescaling; move the \sqrt{4\pi} out of the generator list and into the per_symbol rider for B (where the entry already states it correctly), keeping the generator list to G, c, M_\text{BH}, \mathcal{M}_\text{unit}.

errors.claim: c_s generator numeric_factor: '1 (sometimes \sqrt{2} for the isothermal-vs-adiabatic c_s)'
errors.problem: The adiabatic and isothermal sound speeds differ by \sqrt{\gamma} (c_{s,\text{ad}}=\sqrt{\gamma P/\rho}, c_{s,\text{iso}}=\sqrt{P/\rho}), not by \sqrt2; \sqrt2 holds only in the special case \gamma=2. The \sqrt2 appears to be imported from the neighbouring scale-height convention (H=c_s/\Omega vs \sqrt2 c_s/\Omega), which the entry lists separately and correctly.
errors.correction: numeric_factor '1 or \sqrt{\gamma} (adiabatic vs isothermal c_s)'; keep the \sqrt2 only on the H definition row.

verdicts.system: Soft-matter / coarse-grained reduced units with electrostatics
Hamiltonian and classical-chaos conventions (m = ω = 1, Lyapunov-time rescaling)

errors.claim: generator 'E \ \text{or}\ \hbar\ \text{or}\ L (third scale, problem-dependent)' with dimension (1, 2, -2, 0, 0)
errors.problem: The single 5-tuple is wrong for two of the three listed alternatives. \hbar and angular momentum L have dimension (1,2,-1,0,0) (action), not (1,2,-2,0,0) (energy). Since m and \omega are already fixed, choosing \hbar rather than E is a different completion of the basis (it sets the action scale, and then E=\hbar\omega is derived), so the alternatives are not interchangeable at fixed dimension.
errors.correction: Split into two generator rows, as the Fermi-units entry does: E with (1,2,-2,0,0), and \hbar or L with (1,2,-1,0,0). Note that with m and \omega already declared, adding both E and \hbar over-determines the (M,L,T) basis and imposes a dimensionless condition (E/\hbar\omega = 1).

errors.claim: continuum Dirac-cone limit written as H = v_F(\sigma_xk_x+\sigma_yk_y) with v_F = 3ta/2\hbar \to 3/2
errors.problem: v_F = 3ta/(2\hbar) uses a = the carbon–carbon bond length (a_{cc} \approx 1.42 Å), whereas this entry's length generator is explicitly declared as 'a (lattice constant)'. For graphene the lattice constant is a = \sqrt3\,a_{cc} \approx 2.46 Å, so in the declared units v_F = \sqrt3\,ta/(2\hbar) \to \sqrt3/2 \approx 0.866, not 3/2. This is exactly the class of silent numeric-factor error the entry says it exists to catch.
errors.correction: With a = lattice constant: v_F = \sqrt3 t a/(2\hbar) \to \sqrt3/2 in a=\hbar=t=1 units; the value 3/2 holds only if the declared length unit is the nearest-neighbour bond length a_{cc}.

errors.claim: V(x) = V_0\sin^2(k_Lx) versus V(x) = \tfrac{V_0}{2}[1-\cos(2k_Lx)] versus V(x) = -\tfrac{V_0}{2}\cos(2k_Lx): peak-to-peak versus amplitude, a factor of 2
errors.problem: No factor of 2 exists among the three forms as written. The first two are literally the same function (\sin^2\theta \equiv (1-\cos2\theta)/2), and the third differs from the second only by the additive constant V_0/2. All three have peak-to-peak depth exactly V_0, so a paper using any of them means the same lattice depth.
errors.correction: The genuine factor-of-2 ambiguity is between depth-convention forms V(x)=V_0\sin^2(k_Lx) (peak-to-peak V_0) and amplitude-convention forms V(x)=V_0\cos(2k_Lx) or -V_0\cos(2k_Lx) (peak-to-peak 2V_0). Replace the third listed form by V_0\cos(2k_Lx) to make the row true; the downstream claim (t and U depend exponentially on \sqrt{s}) is fine.

errors.claim: per_symbol: 'factor-of-2 ambiguity in every quoted cooperativity C = g^2/(\kappa\gamma) versus 4g^2/(\kappa\gamma)' vs fingerprint: 'cooperativity C = g^2/(\kappa\gamma) or 2g^2/(\kappa\gamma) quoted as the figure of merit'
errors.problem: The entry states two different partner conventions for the same quantity in two places (4g^2/\kappa\gamma in per_symbol, 2g^2/\kappa\gamma in fingerprints), so at least one row is wrong as a description of the ambiguity it is meant to encode.
errors.correction: Fix a single κ/γ definition and state the pair consistently: with \kappa,\gamma as energy-decay (FWHM) rates the common pair is C = g^2/(\kappa\gamma) and C = 4g^2/(\kappa\gamma); the form 2g^2/(\kappa\gamma) arises when \gamma denotes the amplitude (\gamma/2) decay. Listing all three without saying which κ/γ convention each assumes is the actual trap.

verdicts.system: Fermi units (ħ = k_F = 1, with m or E_F set to 1)
Dimensionless-generator declarations (little-h units, "units where Re = 1", α = 1)

errors.claim: 'the h-exponent is +3 here [P(k) in h^{-3}Mpc^3], -1 for lengths, +1 for masses (M_\odot/h), +2 for surface densities — there is no single h-power for the system'
errors.problem: The list mixes two opposite sign conventions and gets the surface-density magnitude wrong. Under one consistent convention (exponent of h appearing in the quoted unit label): lengths h^{-1}Mpc → -1; masses h^{-1}M_\odot → -1 (the entry says +1, contradicting its own parenthetical M_\odot/h); P(k) in h^{-3}Mpc^3 → -3 (the entry says +3); surface density h^{-1}M_\odot/(h^{-1}Mpc)^2 = h\,M_\odot Mpc^{-2} → +1 (the entry says +2). Under the opposite (value-multiplier) convention all signs flip together, so no convention makes the quoted list self-consistent.
errors.correction: Using the unit-label convention: lengths -1, masses -1, P(k) -3, surface densities +1 (the standard weak-lensing unit is h\,M_\odot\,pc^{-2}), densities +2, H_0 +1, \sigma_8 and n_s 0. The structural point — the exponent must be tabulated per symbol, not derived from dimensions — is correct and survives the fix.

missing_systems: Rotating / geophysical scaling (f-plane and quasi-geostrophic nondimensionalization): lengths by L, time by f^{-1} or the advective L/U, depth by H, with Rossby Ro=U/(fL), Ekman Ek=\nu/(fL^2), Burger Bu=(NH/fL)^2 and the \beta-plane parameter as residues. Named in entry 1's 'used_in' but never enumerated, though it is the default convention of the entire GFD literature.

Rotating-convection / geodynamo units: shell gap d as length; time chosen as viscous d^2/\nu, magnetic d^2/\eta, or the rotational \Omega^{-1}; B scaled by \sqrt{\rho\mu_0\eta\Omega} (Elsasser scaling) or \sqrt{\rho\mu_0}\,\Omega d. Residues Ek, Ra, Pm, \Lambda. The Christensen et al. dynamo-benchmark convention is a de facto standard and differs from both Boussinesq entries here.

Kolmogorov (dissipation-scale) units: \eta=(
u^3/\varepsilon)^{1/4}, u_\eta=(
u\varepsilon)^{1/4}, 	au_\eta=(
u/\varepsilon)^{1/2}. Distinct from both the outer scaling and the box units, and the convention in which most DNS small-scale statistics are actually reported.

Lattice-gauge-theory lattice units: a=1 with \hbar=c=1, dimensionless bare coupling \beta=6/g^2, masses and momenta as am and ap, scale set a posteriori by r_0, w_0, t_0 or f_\pi. This is the QFT sibling of the condensed-matter a=\hbar=t=1 entry and has its own 'restoration' problem (scale setting) that the enumeration never addresses.

Gravitational-action normalizations in holography / string theory: 16\pi G=1 (equivalently 2\kappa^2=1), AdS radius \ell=1, \alpha'=1 or \ell_s=1, sometimes with an extra L_{AdS}=1 layered on G=c=1. These change the Einstein-equation coefficient away from the 8\pi assumed throughout the GR entries and are exactly the 8\pi-vs-16\pi trap the brief asks about.

Lattice-Boltzmann lattice units: \delta x=\delta t=1, lattice speed c=1, c_s^2=1/3, viscosity tied to the relaxation time by \nu=(\tau-1/2)c_s^2, conversion to physical units via independent \Delta x, \Delta t and \Delta\rho. One of the most widely used 'code units' systems in computational fluids, with residues (lattice Mach and Knudsen numbers) that must never be restored.

Circular restricted three-body / astrodynamics canonical units: G(m_1+m_2)=1, separation a=1, mean motion n=1 (period 2\pi), leaving the mass ratio \mu as the only parameter; the two-body 'DU/TU' canonical units with \mu_\oplus=1 are the same convention in orbital mechanics.

Lane–Emden / polytrope scaling in stellar structure: r=\alpha\xi, \rho=\rho_c\theta^n, \alpha^2=(n+1)K\rho_c^{1/n-1}/(4\pi G) — a per-problem scaling whose length generator depends on the central density and the EOS constant, and the standard nondimensionalization of every stellar-structure and TOV-polytrope paper (K=100 is quoted in the NR entry without ever defining its convention).

Homogeneous-GPE healing-length units: \xi=\hbar/\sqrt{2mgn} (or \hbar/\sqrt{mgn} — a genuine \sqrt2 convention trap), sound speed c=\sqrt{gn/m}, time \xi/c or \hbar/(gn), \psi normalized to \sqrt{n}. Used throughout vortex-dynamics and quantum-turbulence work and structurally different from the trap-units entry (no \omega, and g is a generator rather than a residue).

Radiative-transfer optical-depth units: the independent variable is d\tau=-\kappa\rho\,ds, intensities in units of B(T) or of the incident flux, with the opacity absorbed into the coordinate itself. A per-field nondimensionalization in which a generator is applied to the coordinate rather than to a field, which the schema never covers.

Diffusion-equation (Fourier) scaling: t^*=\alpha t/L^2, Fourier number Fo, Biot number Bi, with the mass-transfer analogues Pe, Sc, Sh and the Stefan number for phase change. The canonical textbook nondimensionalization of heat and mass transfer; entry 2 covers only its momentum analogue.

Combustion / flame units: laminar flame thickness \delta_L=\alpha/s_L and speed s_L as the length and velocity generators, temperature by (T_b-T_u), with Zel'dovich number \beta, Damköhler and Karlovitz numbers as residues; also the Arrhenius activation-energy asymptotics scaling.

Reaction–diffusion and mathematical-biology nondimensionalization: Michaelis–Menten quasi-steady-state scaling (Segel–Slemrod), Turing systems reduced to a domain-size parameter \gamma and a diffusion ratio d, epidemic models scaled to R_0. The largest single literature that nondimensionalizes per paper, and entirely absent.

Practical MD/chemistry code-unit systems that absorb nothing: GROMACS (nm, ps, u, kJ/mol, e, bar), LAMMPS 'real' and 'metal' unit sets, CHARMM kcal/mol/Å. These are the molecular analogue of the Gadget UnitLength/UnitMass/UnitVelocity entry — pure numerical rescalings with every constant surviving — and the LJ entry covers only 'units lj'.

Self-similar / similarity-variable scalings: Blasius \eta=y\sqrt{U/(\nu x)}, Sedov–Taylor \xi=r/(Et^2/\rho)^{1/5}, Barenblatt intermediate asymptotics. The 'unit' depends on an independent variable, so it is neither a constant generator nor an affine map — a fourth structural failure mode the family notes do not list.

Hybrid-code / ion-scale plasma units: lengths in the ion inertial length d_i=c/\omega_{pi}, time in \Omega_{ci}^{-1}, velocities in v_A, B in B_0 (the standard normalization of reconnection and space-plasma hybrid codes). Mentioned only in passing in the PIC entry's fingerprints, though it is a distinct preset with its own residues (\beta_i, m_i/m_e absent by construction, \Omega_{ci}/\omega_{pi}).
overall: Unusually strong enumeration: 14 of 25 entries survive independent recomputation with every dimension 5-tuple, numeric factor, per-symbol relation and benchmark equation correct. I recomputed all generator tuples and found exactly one wrong (entry 18's 'E or ħ or L' given an energy tuple when ħ/L are action, (1,2,-1,0,0)); tesla (1,0,-2,0,-1), μ0 (1,1,-2,0,-2), ε0 (-1,-3,4,0,2), charge (0,0,1,0,1), specific R (0,2,-2,-1,0) and β2 (0,-1,2,0,0) are all right. I independently re-derived and confirm: √(Pr/Ra) and 1/√(RaPr) in free-fall RBC; the Pr^{-1}/Ra diffusive form and √(RaPr) velocity map; Ra_c = 1707.762 / 657.511; Hénon R_v=1, t_cr=2√2, det(G,M,E)=2; det(ħ,k_F,E_F)=1 with E_F=1/2 vs m=1/2; E_R kinetic prefactor 1 vs trap-units 1/2; g=4πNa_s/a_ho; ρ_unit=c^6/G^3M^2≈6.18e17 g/cm^3 and 1.47662 km / 4.92549 μs; G_code=43007.1 with h cancelling and [T]=0.978 Gyr/h; ∇²ψ=-4πℓ_B ρ_q against βu=ℓ_B q q/r; Ising-vs-spin-1/2 factor 4 with 2.269→0.567; W=4t/8t/12t; Agrawal's i∂_ξU=(sgn β2/2)∂_τ²U-N²|U|²U with T_FWHM/1.763 and z_0=(π/2)L_D; GS2's √2 and v̂_th=√(T̂/m̂); HARM β=2p/b², σ=b²/ρ. Errors cluster in four places: (1) two internal contradictions in the viscous-NS entry (a pressure scale invoking a non-generator U, and a Re-on-LHS fingerprint that belongs to convective time units — the declared (L,ν,ρ) set makes every coefficient 1); (2) numeric-factor rows that are self-cancelling or misattributed (two 'incompatible' compressible pressure normalizations that are algebraically identical; three optical-lattice potentials that are the same function up to an additive constant; √2 where √γ belongs in the shearing box; h-exponents with mixed signs and a wrong surface-density power); (3) one benchmark equation that is genuinely wrong (the PIC Coulomb form omits the surviving 1/(4π n_0 d_e³) plasma-parameter residue), plus a dropped 1/e in the otherwise-correct PIC Gauss-law derivation; (4) two schema_fit misclassifications (Boussinesq free-fall, whose own notes describe an affine offset; GRMHD, which carries the same B/√4π rescaling that earned the Newtonian MHD entry a needs_symbol_rescaling verdict, and which smuggles in a dimensionless generator the enumeration elsewhere declares unsupportable). Secondary weakness: sourcing. Hénon units, Fermi units, lattice CM units, NLS and the chaos entry all cite the Buckingham-π Wikipedia page, which supports none of their specific numeric claims — those entries happen to be correct, but they are unverified by their own citations. Coverage is fluid/plasma/astro-heavy and thin on diffusion-dominated, reacting, rotating/geophysical, lattice-field-theory and similarity-variable conventions.
